raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 45 years, so I don't think too hard — I mostly do what worked last year. Let me talk through how I'll split my 16.1 mu.

Most of my land, about 12 mu, stays on the wheat-maize rotation like everyone around me. That's what the well is for — you can't reliably get a wheat crop here without pumping water 3 or 4 times over winter and spring. The rest I split into small plots: 1 mu cotton near the road, 1 mu millet on the drier corner, 1 mu mung bean, and 1.1 mu peanut on the sandier patch. Millet and mung bean don't pay much but my wife and I eat them, and peanut sells okay at the village market.

For wheat I buy two bags of 15-15-15 compound per mu before sowing, then topdress with about half a bag of urea at green-up. That comes out around 22 kg nitrogen per mu. My neighbor old Wang tried cutting back two years ago and his yield dropped, so I don't change it — a bad wheat harvest is a disaster, wasting a bit of fertilizer is just money. Improved variety seed from the town dealer, same one I've used four years running.

Summer maize goes straight in after wheat harvest, no-till with the seeder. Hybrid seed — everybody uses hybrid for maize now, the old kinds don't yield. Less fertilizer than wheat since the soil still has some left, maybe 18 kg N.

Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm is bad most years, I spray 4 or 5 times. It's work but the price per jin is good.

Millet, mung bean, peanut I don't fuss with — traditional seed I save myself for millet and mung bean, little fertilizer, one or two sprays. Legumes make their own nitrogen, my father told me that and it's true.
